Pokagon Band of Potawatomi Indians

The Pokagon Band of Potawatomi Indians maintains a community account of homeland continuity, removal pressures and the later reaffirmation of its federal relationship. Its history is particular to Pokagon people, rather than interchangeable with every Potawatomi community. A second reading follows Simon Pokagon’s1898 letter through the Chicago History Museum and the attributed interpretation of Pokagon historian John Low. The historical portrait accompanies that named person’s writing; it is not a portrait of the current government or all Band citizens.

Historical portrait of Simon Pokagon
Photographer unidentified · Chicago History Museum · Public domain

Source & image record ↗ · Public domain — Chicago History Museum’s explicit portrait-specific caption

A museum-identified portrait of the named historical Potawatomi writer, not a portrait of the current Pokagon government or every Band citizen. The caption identifies its publication context as The City Beyond the White City: Simon Pokagon and The Red Man’s Rebuke/the Red Man’s Greeting, but does not name photographer or photograph date. Explicit Public domain statement applies to this portrait only, not other article images. Exact available full-frame JPEG copied unchanged; CSS crops and overlays affect card/backdrop display only.

01

A community-published history

The selected History section and introductory culture paragraphs explain the Band’s own account of continuity. The original inspection scope and date are preserved; linked videos and detailed ritual or clan material are not being reviewed as additional works.

Read the sources [1] Pokagon Band of Potawatomi

02

A named writer and an archival question

The museum presents an1898 Simon Pokagon letter and explains how it informs debate about his authorship. Its transcription and John Low’s interpretation are distinguishable from independent examination of the original manuscript or a complete review of Pokagon’s books.

Our Culture / Neshnabé bmadzëwen — History ↗

Publication: Undated; footer year is not treated as publication date

Substantive public history from a particular Potawatomi government. Useful for differences within related peoples and continuity through removal pressures. Legal summaries, casualty estimates and court details are not independently established here. Other ritual and clan sections are outside the selected synthesis.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual History section, web lines 511–522, and introductory culture paragraphs 499–503. Linked videos, archives and other sections not claimed as reviewed works.

Review recorded: October 21, 2026

Simon Pokagon Letter: Voice of a Potawatomi Leader (November4,2024) ↗

The museum introduces an1898 Simon Pokagon letter and competing interpretations of his literary authorship. It includes attributed perspectives from Pokagon historian John Low; the letter transcription is distinct from a fresh manuscript examination.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Visible article body74–108 and displayed letter transcription110–131 read, plus portrait-specific Public domain caption81. The donated original letter, linked books, underlying research and separately permission-credited exposition photograph were not inspected or reproduced.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
